code.description: Machine-readable refusal code. `stale-id` reports a numeric symbol id or rule index whose `snapshot` does not match the served program's generation — either absent or issued by an earlier program. Re-issue the id from a current response's `snapshot` and id members, or address by declared name.

snapshot.description: Present on `analyze` and `inspect`: the program generation that issued the ids in `result` (#595).

Snapshot.description: The served program's generation (#595): increments each time a program snapshot is adopted — the initial load, every content-changing reload, and recovery after a failed load. Every response that issues numeric `symbol`/`rule` addresses reports it, and a request carrying a numeric address must send that value back or be refused `stale-id`. It is a generation counter, not a content digest — `inputIdentity` keeps its own semantics. A request whose addresses are all declared names ignores it.

address.description: The rule's canonical address (ADR-0035): the bare declared `NAME` when it selects this rule unambiguously, otherwise `NAME#N` in declaration order (`#N` for unnamed rules). Passing it back selects the same rule — or fails `ambiguous-rule` when no unambiguous spelling exists.

event.description: The rule's event binding: a canonical event id, or `subroutine:<name>` for a subroutine rule.

content.description: Present when `content` was requested: the owner's `workshop-rs/rule-content-v1` document. Each condition and action also carries `span` when the program has one.

owningRule.description: The owning rule's identity — `{id, name, address, span}` like a `rules` list entry — so a consumer renders a rule location without a second lookup (#792); null when the reference has no owning rule. `address` is the canonical rule address (ADR-0035).

expression.description: The canonical spelling of the repeated expression.

count.description: How many times the expression is evaluated.

spanKind.description: Whether the finding's `span` is the expression's own span or the enclosing loop action's span (#791).

location.description: Source path and 1-based line/column; full spans are available through findings.

ruleAddress.description: The owning rule's canonical address (ADR-0035) — `NAME` or `NAME#N`; reusable as a `rule`/`--rule` selector.

repeated.description: The `RepeatedValue` facts on a `repeated-value` finding; null otherwise (#791).

inputIdentity.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the input's primary entry source (the provider's `sourceIdentity` for provider projects). For a single-file input it covers the whole input; for a provider directory project it hashes only the entry file, so member-file edits do not change it — use `stale-id` refusals for freshness, not this value.

sourceFiles.description: The loaded input's source files in canonical file-id order — file 0 is the entry source; entries are display paths.

settings.description: The program's settings block projected read-only (#836): section and member names with scalar values — `null` when the program declares no settings block.

name.description: The section or member name — canonical for catalogued settings, authored otherwise.

value.description: The member's scalar value as emitted text (`On`/`Off` for booleans). Absent on section nodes.

children.description: A section's members. Absent on leaf nodes.

unavailable.description: ADR-0024: result members the result should carry but cannot for this input. `names` names the owner that must serve target-language spellings (today `opy-rs` for an OverPy input, until its provider capability exists); raw Workshop results carry no `unavailable`.

byCode.description: Per-code finding counts over the filtered set before `max` truncation (#791); omitted when the set has no coded findings.

next.description: Shared follow-up commands rendered as `next:` records (#792); each entry is a complete `wright` command line.

byCode.description: Per-code counts over the full list before this cap (#791); omitted for lists whose items carry no `code`.

callerAddress.description: The calling rule's canonical address (ADR-0035); reusable as the `caller` filter.

emittedBytes.description: Emitted artifact size in bytes; null when emission fails — emittedBytesUnavailable names the reason (ADR-0030 decision 3: unknown is not a value).

total.description: Canonical element total; absent when the count cannot run — elementCountUnavailable names the reason. The budget still reports even when the count is unavailable.

address.description: The rule's canonical address (ADR-0035); reusable as `costEstimate`'s `rule`.

skipped.description: Rule evaluations the configured registry skipped (canonical CFG unavailable) — the same disclosure `lint` carries (#788).

transaction.description: The transaction the service assembled from the statement edits — present when the edits could be planned, so the caller can apply or replay it through its own write path.

preview.description: Each edited source after the transaction — present when the transaction validates, like `validateEditTransaction`.

returns.description: Optional: the owner-declared return type of a value, in the same vocabulary as parameter types.

variadic.description: Optional: present as true when the callable's last parameter repeats for extra arguments.

total.description: Entries the request lists across all pages.

nextCursor.description: Opaque; present when more entries follow. Pass it back as `cursor` with the same request.

AthenaTrace.description: The unchanged `athena` trace (ADR-0033). `athena` owns this contract — see `athena`'s simulator-interface document — and evolves it under its own versioning; Wright does not reinterpret or reorder it. `outcome` says how the run ended; `logs`, `globals`, `players`, and `hud` describe the state when the run ended and must be read only after checking `outcome.status`. `missingInputs` lists the live inputs a scenario did not supply; `expectations` reports one result per scenario expectation.

outcome.description: How the run ended: `{"status":"complete"}` for the whole requested time, `{"status":"not_modeled","construct":…,"tick":…}` when the run stopped at a construct the simulator does not model, or `{"status":"missing_input"}` when it stopped at a live input the scenario did not supply. `not_modeled` and `missing_input` are trace content, not failures; `tick` is absent when the stop preceded the first tick.

written_to.description: The file the program was written to.

input_identity.description: The loaded input's primary entry source digest — same semantics as `project.inputIdentity`.

program.description: The loaded program's summary — the same members `analyze`'s `program` reports (#792).

next.description: Shared follow-up commands rendered as `next:` records (#792); each entry is a complete `wright` command line.

result_schemas.description: The committed-schema definition describing each advertised operation's result (#532): operation name to its `#/$defs/<Op>Result` reference.

athena_version.description: The `athena` release `simulate` links against (ADR-0033) — the owner of the trace format it returns.

Sources.description: Source name → full current text. On `validateEditTransaction` the key is the loaded input's source spelling and the field may be omitted (the service reads the named files from disk, #472). On `providerValidateEdit` the keys are `documents` URIs covering every `edits[].source` — an edit into an unsupplied source refuses `edit-unknown-source`. The text is the precondition each edit's `source_identity` verifies against and the text edits apply to.

EditRange.description: A half-open source range in 1-based lines and character columns; `end` is exclusive and a column may point one past the line's last character. A zero-width range inserts `new_text`.

kind.description: The edit kind: `edit` for a caller-proposed replacement; other kinds may appear on service-computed results.

source.description: The source this edit applies to: the loaded input's spelling on `validateEditTransaction`, or a `documents` URI key on the provider operations.

source_identity.description: The SHA-256 hex digest of the source's current text — the same digest `project.inputIdentity` reports for the entry source; a text that hashes differently refuses `edit-stale-source`.

new_text.description: The replacement text; empty deletes the range.

edits.description: The transaction's edits, applied atomically; edits in one source must not overlap, and two zero-width edits at the same position refuse `edit-zero-width-conflict`.

uri.description: The document's URI — also its key in `documents`; provider edit results address documents by it.

version.description: The document's current version; provider-computed edits validated against another version refuse `edit-stale-source`.

DocumentSet.description: URI → `Document` map: the caller-owned project document set the provider operates on. `providerValidateEdit` refuses an `edits[].source` outside the set with `edit-unknown-source`.

output.description: File to write the program to; default `<entry stem>.ow` in the service's working directory.

force.description: Replace an existing output file. The service never prompts, so a repeat compile to the same file needs force: true. The input source file is never overwritten.

to.description: Output locale for the emitted Workshop text (e.g. "en-US", "zh-CN"); defaults to the loaded input's locale. Use it to convert Workshop text between client locales independently of the input locale.

rule.description: A rule address (`NAME` or `NAME#N`, ADR-0035) selects that rule's element-cost drill-down (#724): `rule` (identity, count, span), `statements[]` (direct children ranked by recursive count) and `byNode[]` (each node's own contribution summed per canonical node name, with occurrences) replace the whole-program `elementCount`/`findings` view. The drill-down reports no findings, so `severity`/`file`/`max` do not apply to it.

sources.description: Optional current texts for the edited sources; omitted or null reads the named files from disk (#472).

language_id.description: The configured source provider's language id — `opy` for the shipped provider.

documents.description: Optional: the caller-owned document set — every `edits[].source` must be a key, and errors in any supplied document block the post-edit check. Omitted or null: the session's loaded project supplies the set — every member read from disk at version 0, keyed by `file://` URI.

sources.description: Optional URI → current text covering every `edits[].source` (omitted or null defaults to each document's text); each edit's `source_identity` verifies against it.

project_root.description: Optional project root the provider resolves the project from.

inputIdentity.description: The freshness precondition (ADR-0029): the `inputIdentity` of the program the statement addresses were read from — the value `project` reports, or the identity of the supplied `sources` text. A mismatch refuses `edit-stale-source`.

sources.description: Optional current text of the loaded input source, keyed by its source spelling: when supplied the program the addresses name is loaded from that text, which is also the precondition each assembled edit's `source_identity` verifies against; omitted or null uses the disk-loaded program.

snapshot.description: Required when any `edits[].rule` is a numeric index: the generation that issued it. Declared rule names ignore it.

edits.description: The statement edits. Every `rule`+`list`+`index` address names a position in the program before any edit in this request applies; two edits at the same address refuse `edit-duplicate-address`.

rule.description: The rule holding the statement list: its index in the program or its rule address (`NAME` or `NAME#N` in declaration order, ADR-0035) — an unknown address is `unknown-rule`, a duplicated bare name `ambiguous-rule`. A numeric index must carry the `snapshot` generation that issued it; a name ignores `snapshot`.

list.description: The statement list inside the rule — the same two lists `rule-content-v1` exports.

index.description: For `insert`, the index the new statements are placed before (`index == list length` appends); for `replace`/`delete`, the index of the statement to change — the flat index space `rules` reports.

change.description: The change to make at the address.

statements.description: Required on `insert`: the `rule-content-v1` statement documents to insert, in order — statements that belong at one position (an `if`, its body, its `end`) go in one insert.

statement.description: Required on `replace`: the replacement `rule-content-v1` statement document.

RuleContentStatement.description: A `workshop-rs/rule-content-v1` statement document — the same node shape `rules` returns in `conditions`/`actions`: `{"value": <value node>}` for a condition, `{"call": "<id>", "args": [...]}` for an action; `disabled` may accompany either. `span`/`spans` keys are output-only and refused.

within.description: An enum domain identity as `lookup` returns it. Required for `enumMember`, refused for other kinds.

cursor.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`; omitted for the first page.

inputIdentity.description: The freshness precondition (ADR-0033): the `inputIdentity` of the program to simulate — the value `project` reports, or the identity of the supplied `sources` text. A mismatch refuses `edit-stale-source` and runs nothing.

sources.description: Optional current text of the loaded input, keyed by its source spelling — the meaning it has for `editStatements`: when supplied the program is loaded from that text and `inputIdentity` is checked against it; omitted or null uses the served program.

seconds.description: Simulated seconds for a scenario-free run — `athena`'s `Options.seconds`. Required when `scenario` is omitted; refused when `scenario` is supplied, since a scenario owns the simulated time.

scenario.description: An `athena` scenario value (ADR-0033): players, injected events, expected observations, and the simulated `seconds`. Passed through uninterpreted; `athena` validates it — a malformed scenario refuses and inputs it omits are reported in the trace, never defaulted. Mutually exclusive with `seconds`.
